html:
The Wolastoqiyik, or Maliseet, are an Algonquian people of the Saint John River valley in New Brunswick, Maine and Quebec. Their name means "people of the beautiful river", from Wolastoq, their name for the Saint John. The Wolastoqiyik Wahsipekuk First Nation is the Maliseet community of Quebec, along the south shore of the Saint Lawrence.

They hunted, fished and farmed along the river and travelled by birchbark canoe. Their language is shared, with small differences, with the Passamaquoddy. With them, the Penobscot, the Abenaki and the Mi'kmaq they formed the Wabanaki Confederacy.

They were allies of New France and fought the English in the colonial wars of the 1600s and 1700s. After the British conquest and the arrival of Loyalists in the 1780s, they were pushed onto small reserves along the river.
